'''Lower Nossob''' is an extinct [[Khoisan language]] once spoken along the [[Nossob River]] on the border of South Africa and Botswana, near Namibia. It was closely related to the [[Taa language|Taa]] language.

There are two attested dialects: {{lang|nsb|ǀʼAuni}} (pronounced {{IPAc-en|ˈ|aʊ|n|i:}} {{respell|OW|nee}}), or {{lang|nsb|ǀʼAuo}}, recorded by [[Dorothea Bleek]], and {{lang|nsb|ǀHaasi}}, recorded by Robert Story. {{lang|nsb|ǀʼAuni}} is the word they formerly used for themselves; {{lang|nsb|ǀʼAuo}} (or {{lang|nsb|ǀʼAu}}) is what they called their language. {{lang|nsb|ǀauni, ǁauni, Auni}} are misspellings.  Other renderings of the name {{lang|nsb|ǀHaasi}} are {{lang|nsb|Kʼuǀha꞉si, Kiǀhasi}}, and {{lang|nsb|Kiǀhazi}}.<ref>{{cite book |first=Yvonne |last=Treis |chapter=Names of Khoisan languages and their variants |title=Language, identity, and conceptualization among the Khoisan |editor-first=Mathias |editor-last=Schladt |publisher=Rüdiger Köppe Verlag |pages=463–503 |year=1998 |isbn=978-3-89645-143-9}}</ref>
